coverage_gaps.reason: Official max-effort capability results and an evaluator GDP.pdf xhigh result are now curated. Additional exact safety results for Spark 1.3 remain uncurated; Wonder Full safety results are not transferred.

Fifteen capability metrics are curated separately for Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, including distinct partial/binary OSWorld scores. Base Wonder safety scores remain unavailable in the extracted card; Full safety results are not transferred.

Exact system-card, Surge GDP.pdf/sudo L7 and Parallel search results are curated. Exact DeepSWE, OSWorld, AutomationBench and Terminal-Bench Science launch-chart values/settings remain unresolved; no relative deltas are converted into scores.

Nine additional explicit release-page results are curated along with existing safety results. Mistral Large 4 remains a preview with unspecified run settings for many rows. Finance/legal and other chart-only results remain pending exact extraction; promised weights are not treated as released.

Six exact OpenRouter model IDs have route-specific price snapshots with tier overrides preserved. Other curated releases have no reconciled route in this snapshot. No usage rows are promoted because mapped IDs did not appear in the captured top-50 daily ranking feed. Absence is censored/unknown, never zero.
Historical coverage now includes selected Claude, Gemini, Llama and Mixtral releases plus GPT-4. This remains a partial catalog, with source-specific protocols preserved.

Official DeepSeek changelog search results show a 10 September 2026 V4.1-Flash release and a benchmark score block, but the page timed out when opened, and its footnote names DeepSeek-V4-Flash while the release title is V4.1-Flash. Exact release-to-score mapping and score units need confirmation before observations are assigned.

The seed has three benchmark variants with at least six distinct releases represented (Terminal-Bench 4.0, DeepSWE v1.1, CursorBench 4.0). No fourth exact variant reaches six releases without combining distinct protocols, reconciling a source conflict, or inferring scores.

Primary-source rows differ materially in task, prompt, and evaluator; this fragment keeps report-specific variants and does not create a unified rank. Tool-use coverage remains sparse outside Llama 3.1 BFCL/Nexus.

The selected primary reports do not provide a sufficiently consistent, numeric safety evaluation matrix for these releases. This fragment excludes unsupported safety scores; the canonical dataset has separate sourced safety evidence.

Versions and reported protocols differ; Gemini 1.5 Table 11 reports May 2024 checkpoints in an arXiv v5 report. Values are retained as report-specific variants, not treated as a controlled longitudinal evaluation.
No missing score is inferred from a neighboring report, model size, or similarly named benchmark. Only explicit report cells are represented; unreported cells remain absent.

OpenAI’s launch page gives only relative claims for DeepSWE v1.1 (+6.4 percentage points over GPT-6 Sol at a lower effort/cost), OSWorld 2.0 (+7 points over GPT-6 Sol at max), Terminal-Bench Science 0.1 (more than doubles GPT-6 Sol at max), and AutomationBench (+4.8 points over GPT-6 Sol at medium). No absolute GPT-6.1 score appears in that page. Current evaluator leaderboards checked on 2026-10-17 did not expose a GPT-6.1 result on DeepSWE or OSWorld; the current AutomationBench list also has no GPT-6.1 row. Do not assign GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, or relative deltas as GPT-6.1 scores.

The OpenAI launch page includes comparative visual material, but no exact, unambiguous numeric GPT-6.1 value was recoverable from the accessible figure text. No values were estimated from bar heights or attributed from GPT-6 Astra. The system-card KernelGen 1P results are likewise discussed but do not provide a score in accessible text; excluded.
